headline.headline: YAMAMOTO FANS 10, DODGERS ONE WIN FROM SWEEPING BRAVES
headline.deck: Hernández homer in fourth inning breaks scoreless duel, LA wins 3-1
headline.body:
ATLANTA — Yoshinobu Yamamoto was untouchable again Tuesday night, striking out 10 Atlanta Braves across seven dominant innings as the Los Angeles Dodgers won Game 3 of the National League Division Series, 3-1, before 42,420 at Truist Park. The Dodgers now stand one victory from eliminating the Braves and advancing to the NLCS.

The game was scoreless through three innings before Kiké Hernández broke the deadlock with a two-run home run in the fourth, giving Yamamoto all the cushion he would need. Freddie Freeman added another run in that decisive frame as the Dodgers plated three runs in a single inning against a Braves staff that had kept pace until the dam broke. Atlanta answered with a lone run in the fifth but never threatened seriously again, with the Dodgers bullpen locking down the final two frames.

Game 4 is set for Wednesday in Atlanta, where the Dodgers will attempt to complete the series sweep. The Braves, who finished the regular season 94-68 and won the NL East, now face elimination at home after failing to manufacture any offense against Yamamoto, who has been the most dominant starting pitcher of this postseason.

secondary.headline: TKACHUK NETS WINNER BUT MARCHAND INJURY CLOUDS PANTHERS' 2-1 VICTORY OVER KINGS
secondary.deck: Veteran forward Brad Marchand hurt as Florida advances in second-round playoff battle
secondary.body:
Matthew Tkachuk scored the decisive goal in the third period Tuesday to lift the Florida Panthers to a 2-1 win over the Los Angeles Kings, but the victory was overshadowed by an injury to veteran forward Brad Marchand that cast uncertainty over Florida's playoff hopes. Marchand, whose toughness and experience have been central to the Panthers' second-round run, did not return after leaving the game.

The severity of Marchand's injury had not been confirmed as of press time, but the concern in the Florida locker room was evident. Tkachuk's goal gave the Panthers the lead and proved to be the difference in a tightly contested game, but the Marchand situation looms large as Florida pushes deeper into a grueling May playoff run.

secondary.headline: PELICANS STUN THUNDER IN OKLAHOMA CITY, 116-110, TO SHAKE UP WESTERN CONFERENCE SEMIFINALS
secondary.deck: New Orleans wins on the road to gain crucial edge in second-round series
secondary.body:
The New Orleans Pelicans traveled to Oklahoma City and left with a 116-110 victory over the Thunder on Tuesday, a result that could tilt the balance of the Western Conference semifinals. The Pelicans, who also saw the Denver Nuggets beat the Utah Jazz 117-106 in another second-round contest, showed they could win in a hostile arena against one of the conference's young powers.

The Thunder, playing at home, could not hold off New Orleans down the stretch as the Pelicans converted enough in the final minutes to secure the six-point margin. The Denver-Utah series also moved decisively in Denver's direction, with the Nuggets pulling away from the Jazz by 11 points in what is shaping up as a commanding performance in that bracket.

secondary.headline: GIANTS RECEIVER BERRIOS TO MISS ENTIRE 2026 SEASON AFTER FOOT SURGERY ANNOUNCEMENT
secondary.deck: Braxton Berrios disclosed the injury Tuesday on Instagram, dealing New York another blow
secondary.body:
New York Giants wide receiver Braxton Berrios announced Tuesday on Instagram that he will undergo season-ending foot surgery, dealing the rebuilding franchise another setback as it prepares for the 2026 NFL season. Berrios made the announcement himself, a sign of how significantly the injury disrupts his availability for the coming campaign.

The Giants, still reshaping their roster following the conclusion of the 2025 season in February, now must find depth at receiver without Berrios, who will miss the full year. The news adds to a busy offseason in which NFL teams across the league continue to retool and re-evaluate their rosters ahead of training camps.

column.headline: YOSHINOBU YAMAMOTO IS MAKING THIS LOOK EASY, AND THAT SHOULD TERRIFY THE REST OF THE NL
column.body:
Ten strikeouts in seven innings. A run allowed that barely registered. Yoshinobu Yamamoto walked into Truist Park on Tuesday night and treated one of the National League's best lineups like a batting practice opponent. The Braves had won 94 games this year and the NL East title. Yamamoto made them look overmatched from the opening pitch, and the Dodgers need one more win to be done with them entirely.

What is most striking is not just the strikeout total but the efficiency and poise of a pitcher who continues to elevate when the stakes are highest. The Dodgers are not winning this series because of depth or luck. They are winning because Yamamoto has given them the kind of ace performance that defines October runs. If Los Angeles does go on to reach the World Series, the conversation about this postseason will begin and end with that right arm.

story.headline: YAMAMOTO SILENCES BRAVES AS DODGERS MOVE ONE WIN FROM NLDS TITLE
story.deck: Hernández and Freeman homers power Los Angeles to 3-1 victory in Atlanta
story.body:
ATLANTA — Yoshinobu Yamamoto struck out 10 batters across seven dominant innings Tuesday night, and a three-run fourth inning was all the Los Angeles Dodgers needed to beat the Atlanta Braves 3-1 at Truist Park before 42,420 fans, putting the Dodgers one victory away from advancing past the National League Division Series.

The scoring came in a concentrated burst. Kiké Hernández launched a two-run homer and Freddie Freeman added a solo shot in the fourth inning to stake Los Angeles to its only lead of the evening, one the Dodgers never relinquished. Atlanta managed just a single run, coming in the fifth inning, and left 14 runners stranded against Yamamoto and the Los Angeles bullpen. The Dodgers themselves stranded 20 baserunners but needed none of them, the game having been decided in that one productive fourth.

Los Angeles, which finished the regular season 100-62, now leads the best-of-five series three games to none heading into Game 4 Wednesday in Atlanta. The Braves, who won the NL East at 94-68, face elimination and will need to win three straight to advance. Meanwhile in the other National League series, the San Diego Padres staved off elimination Tuesday with a 4-3 victory over Milwaukee, with Jake Cronenworth hitting a homer and reliever D. Hall earning the win to force a deciding Game 4.

story.headline: WARRIORS ROUT LAKERS IN SEASON OPENER AS GOLDEN STATE ROLLS TO 26-POINT WIN
story.deck: Stephen Curry and company dismantle Los Angeles in a dominant Chase Center statement.
story.body:
SAN FRANCISCO — The Golden State Warriors wasted no time sending a message to the rest of the Western Conference, dismantling the Los Angeles Lakers 124-98 Tuesday night at Chase Center in what amounted to a wire-to-wire demolition of their longtime rivals. The 26-point margin was no fluke, as Golden State controlled the game from the opening tip and never allowed Los Angeles a foothold at any point in the contest.

The Brooklyn Nets delivered a similarly lopsided verdict on the East Coast, throttling the Charlotte Hornets 124-90 in Charlotte for a 34-point road thrashing. Brooklyn's offense ran smoothly all night, and the Hornets could find no answer as the deficit swelled through each successive quarter.

Elsewhere around the league, the New Orleans Pelicans edged the Oklahoma City Thunder 116-110 in what was the night's tightest contest, with Oklahoma City pushing the visitors all the way to the final buzzer at Paycom Center. The Denver Nuggets also picked up a road win, dispatching the Utah Jazz 117-106 in Salt Lake City to give Nikola Jokic and the defending contenders a confident early-season footing heading into the week.

story.headline: LAFRENIÈRE ERUPTS FOR HAT TRICK AS RANGERS ROLL TO FOURTH STRAIGHT WIN
story.deck: New York star nets three goals, adds assist in dominant showing over rival Islanders
story.body:
Alexis Lafrenière put on a show Tuesday night, recording a hat trick and an assist as the New York Rangers dispatched the crosstown rival New York Islanders for their fourth consecutive victory. Lafrenière, who buried two of his three goals into an empty net, was the unquestioned engine of a Rangers offense that has now found a dangerous rhythm through the early weeks of the 2026-27 NHL season.

The Rangers' four-game winning streak places them among the hottest teams in the league heading into mid-October. Lafrenière's performance against the Islanders was the kind of outburst that changes the conversation around a player, a deep-dive into the net multiple times in a rivalry game that carries its own electric charge regardless of standings or record.

Elsewhere around the league Tuesday, Matthew Tkachuk scored a third-period goal to lift the Florida Panthers past the Los Angeles Kings 2-1, though the victory came at a cost — Brad Marchand left the game injured, and his status going forward remains a significant concern for Florida. Tonight's slate features Utah Mammoth at Boston, San Jose at St. Louis, and Vancouver visiting Carolina, where the Hurricanes will look to slow a Canucks squad riding Taylor Hall's recent two-goal performance.

story.headline: QUARTERBACKS ON THE MOVE AS NFL TEAMS RESHAPE ROSTERS FOR 2026
story.deck: A wave of signal-caller transactions is redefining the league's landscape this spring.
story.body:
The NFL offseason has turned into a quarterback carousel, with several franchises making bold moves to secure their futures under center just months after the Philadelphia Eagles hoisted the Lombardi Trophy at Super Bowl LX. The Las Vegas Raiders struck first among the biggest movers, acquiring a veteran starter via trade while the New York Giants continued negotiations with free-agent options after a forgettable 2025 campaign left the franchise searching for stability at the most important position in professional football.

The April draft reshuffled the deck further, as three quarterbacks were selected in the first round, drawing immediate comparisons to the loaded 2024 class. Tennessee Titans general manager ran the clock on draft night before locking in their pick at No. 1 overall, while scouts from nearly every team burned midnight oil evaluating which prospects were worth the investment. Player agents have reported a frenzy of calls from teams willing to trade future capital to move up and secure a young arm before the window closed.

With organized team activities beginning across the league, several training camp storylines are already taking shape. Wide receivers demanding new contracts, offensive linemen switching teams after the free-agency frenzy in March, and defensive coordinators installing new schemes have front offices working overtime. League observers note the salary cap increase for 2026 gave teams additional flexibility, fueling one of the more aggressive offseasons in recent memory.
